# failure-facts

## Type Aliases

### FailureFacts

```ts
type FailureFacts = object;
```

What a failure says about itself without its message: classes and places, never
text.

#### Properties

##### storageCategory?

```ts
optional storageCategory?: string;
```

A closed category read from the message of a driver or storage error.

##### errorCode?

```ts
optional errorCode?: string;
```

A driver's own error code (ECONNRESET, a Postgres SQLSTATE), never text.

##### emptyMessage?

```ts
optional emptyMessage?: true;
```

The error had no message at all, so there is nothing more to name.

##### thrownAt?

```ts
optional thrownAt?: string;
```

Where it was thrown: the first stack frame, never the message.

### FailureChain

```ts
type FailureChain = FailureFacts & object;
```

One error and its causes as an event may carry them: class, facts, nested cause.

#### Type Declaration

| Name     | Type                            | Description                                                     |
| -------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`   | `"error"` \| `"non-error"`      | `error` for an Error, `non-error` for anything else thrown.     |
| `name?`  | `string`                        | The error class, so a bare failure still says what kind it was. |
| `cause?` | [`FailureChain`](#failurechain) | The error this one wraps, to three levels.                      |

## Functions

### describeFailureFacts()

```ts
function describeFailureFacts(cause, located): FailureFacts;
```

The facts of one error that are safe to write down: a closed category, the
driver's code, whether the message was empty and the throwing frame (the last
three only when `located`: an event that must name a bare failure). Callers add
the error's name and its nested cause.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      |
| --------- | --------- |
| `cause`   | `Error`   |
| `located` | `boolean` |

#### Returns

[`FailureFacts`](#failurefacts)

### describeFailureChain()

```ts
function describeFailureChain(cause, depth?): FailureChain;
```

[describeFailureFacts](#describefailurefacts) for an error and its nested
causes, always located. It never throws: a getter on the error that throws
(name, stack, message, cause) costs that one fact, not the answer its caller is
giving.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Default value |
| --------- | --------- | ------------- |
| `cause`   | `unknown` | `undefined`   |
| `depth`   | `number`  | `0`           |

#### Returns

[`FailureChain`](#failurechain)
